questions.explanation: Given that - Total distance is divided into 3 equal parts (each 1/3 of total distance)First 1/3 : V1 = 10 km/hrSecond 1/3 : V2 = 20 km/hrThird 1/3 : V3 = 60 km/hr Let the total distance be DEach part = D/3Step 1 : Calculate time for each partFor first part : t1 = distance/speed = (D/3)10 = D/30 hoursFor second part : t2 = distance/speed = (D/3)20 = D/60 hoursFor third part : t3 = distance/speed = (D/3)60 = D/180 hoursStep 2 : Calculate total timeTotal time = t1+t2+t3 = D/30 + D/60 + D/180= 6D/180 + 3D/180 + D/180= (6D + 3D + D)/180= 10D/180 = D/18 hoursStep 3 : Calculate average speedAverage speed = Total distance/Total time= D(D/18)= D × 18/D= 18 km/hrAnswer : (A) 18 km/hrThe average speed of the car is 18 km/hr.

The correct statement from the following is
options: A body having zero velocity will not necessarily have zero acceleration
A body having zero velocity will necessarily have zero acceleration
A body having uniform speed can have only uniform acceleration
A body having non-uniform velocity will have zero acceleration
questions.explanation: Statement A: A body having zero velocity will not necessarily have zero acceleration. This is true. For example, at the highest point of a vertically thrown ball: v = 0 but a = g Statement B: A body having zero velocity will necessarily have zero acceleration. False. Statement C: A body having uniform speed can have only uniform acceleration. False. In uniform circular motion, speed is constant but acceleration changes direction continuously. Statement D: A body having non-uniform velocity will have zero acceleration. False. Non-uniform velocity implies acceleration is non-zero. Correct option: A

questions.question: Figure shows the graph of the {x} -co-ordinate of a particle going along the {x} -axis as function of time. Find the instantaneous speed of particle at t=12.5 {~s}( in {m} / {s})
questions.explanation: From the graph, we can read off the piecewiseconstant slope (velocity) in each segment: t=0 to t=4, {~s}: x rises linearly from 0 m to 4 m , so velocity =+1 {~m} / {s} . t=4 to t=8, {~s}: x is constant at 4 m , so velocity =0 . t=8 to t=12, {~s}: x rises linearly from 4 m to 8 m , so velocity =+1 {~m} / {s} . t=12 to t=16, {~s}: x decreases linearly from 8 m to 0 m , so velocity =-2 {~m} / {s} . At t=12.5, {~s} , the motion is in the last segment, where velocity is -2 {~m} / {s} . Hence the instantaneous speed (magnitude of velocity) is |-2|=2 {~m} / {s}
